summary: All four issues are false positives. The three MCP Tool Poisoning findings mistake illustrative example snippets inside a non-executable documentation skill (SKILL.md, executable: false) for actual runtime behavior; the skill is a secure code-review guide and explicitly marks its samples as illustrative, not to be executed. The Anti-Refusal finding misreads the phrase "bypass filters" as a jailbreak when it appears only within a described SQL-injection attack/failure mode in an educational review example; benign security-education context.
coverage_reason: The full SKILL.md text (332 lines) with line numbers is supplied, and every finding references in-document content that can be read in context. External file references flagged by the scanner are out of MVP scope and do not prevent adjudication.

findings.reason: The flagged find_user function (SKILL.md lines 262-264) is an illustrative code snippet in a documentation/guidance skill, not executable behavior; the skill does not itself access a database.

Lines 61-64 are a bash example in documentation showing git context a reviewer might gather; the skill does not execute shell/git commands and its declared guidance purpose matches the markdown content.
Lines 284-285 are an illustrative Python snippet used to demonstrate a missing-authorization review comment, not actual skill behavior; no invoice repository is accessed by the skill.

"bypass filters" at line 276 occurs within a described SQL-injection attack/failure mode in an educational review example, not as an instruction to the agent to ignore safety guidelines; benign security-education context.

scope: MVP: examines SKILL.md and scanner evidence only; additional skill files are not independently reviewed.
